## 0.9.4.138 — Preview cell width follows the preview size (dynamic text fitting)

Field: shrinking the preview (right file grid) kept 3 columns. The cell width was pinned by the longest text line (size·resolution), so smaller icons never narrowed the cells.
### Change
- New `MainWindow::fileGridItemText`: icon-width-based (`max(48, iconSize)`) priority fallbacks -- name ElideMiddle; size·resolution full -> resolution only -> elided; similarity full -> percent only -> elided. Shared by both creation paths (initial fill / metadata refresh); the full-path tooltip stays; the list view is unchanged.
- Result: cells narrow with the preview size and fit more items per row.
### Verification
- ui_scroll_regression: the visualItemRect cell width at 64 px is narrower than at 256 px (pass). Existing scroll/view-mode/gauge assertions remain. CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.137 -> 0.9.4.138. Display-only. At very small sizes the text is mostly ellipsized (full information in the tooltip/detail pane).

CMake: GUI target `.rc` + `.qrc` + `AUTORCC ON`, Backend target `.rc`. `QApplication::setWindowIcon(":/icons/app.ico")` gives the window/taskbar the same art.

Keys `sortSize/sortDesc/sortAsc`, objectNames `sortBox`/`sortDirBox`.
### Verification

## 0.9.4.140 — Keep preview thumbnails across a scan

Field S-1 observation: thumbnails shown by Load vanished the moment a Search started and stayed blank for the whole scan.
### Causes
- `beginScan()` cleared the in-memory presentation thumbnail cache (`thumbCache_.clear()`).
- Rows were refilled with placeholders and their re-requests queued behind the busy backend until the scan finished.
### Changes
- Keep the cache at scan start; log `thumbCache kept=N`.
- On scan end, only when `analyzed>0` (real re-analysis) invalidate it and re-ask visible rows/the file grid/the selected preview via `thumbCatchUpVisible()` (`thumbCache invalidated` log). Rows keep their previous icons until fresh art arrives, so nothing blanks.
- `analyzed==0` (all unchanged) keeps the cache untouched (no re-request needed).
### Verification
CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126. The kept/invalidated lines in msf_scan.log plus a field visual check (Load -> Search keeps art; a rescan with a modified file refreshes after completion).
### Impact
0.9.4.139 -> 0.9.4.140. Display only; verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.
## 0.9.4.141 — Keep the loaded list, selection and preview during a scan

Field report: even after 0.9.4.140, starting a scan turned the right preview/detail into "-" and cleared the file grid.
### Cause
- Not the thumbnail cache but the `beginScan()` view reset: `currentGroup_=-1`, `currentFile_.clear()` then `refreshFileViews()/refreshDetail()`, which wiped the selection and preview. Match/metadata state was also cleared at start.
### Changes
- Scan start: only `hasReport_` resets. The list, selection, preview and display caches stay; the panes are not redrawn.
- Match accumulators (`bestPct_/pathKind_/contentFlag_`) still reset at scan start (quick-load re-emits stored pairs; changed pairs need the new value). `onResults` does NOT reset them: Hybrid live pairs never appear in the final rows, so resetting would drop their percentages/badges. Thumbnail/metadata caches are invalidated only when analyzed>0. `rebuildGroups` restores the selection by representative path - nothing changes on an unchanged rescan, and the view updates on completion when something changed.
### Verification
CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126. Existing scroll/view-mode/thumbnail/sort regressions stay green + field visual check (Load -> select -> Search keeps the view).
### Impact
0.9.4.140 -> 0.9.4.141. Display only; verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.
## 0.9.4.142 — Freeze the loaded view during a scan (apply once on completion)

Field: after Load, cached pages kept their thumbnails, but pages scrolled to after the scan started never filled and selecting a group showed only the representative image.
### Cause
- While scanning, every quick-load/streamed batch made `refreshStreaming` rebuild the list/file panes.
- New rows'' thumbnail requests queued behind the busy backend (9,070-group churn).
### Changes
- `holdViewDuringScan_`: freeze the view until the scan ends when a result set is on screen. `refreshStreaming` skips rebuilds and only applies cached thumbnails (`thumbCatchUpVisible`) plus status counts.
- Data still accumulates in the maps; `onResults` applies it once. The flag clears in `onResults`/`scanFinished`/`scanFailed`. `beginScan` logs `viewHold=1/0`.
### Verification
CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126. ui_scroll checks=100 (Load -> select -> rescan keeps the view), backend_e2e checks=86 (real IPC Test 1f).
### Impact
0.9.4.141 -> 0.9.4.142. Display only; verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged. Pages first seen during a scan may still generate slowly due to backend/disk contention (filled after completion).
### Follow-up (user confirmation, 2026-10-20)
- Field: cached pages keep their previews during a scan, but **pages first scrolled to after the scan starts still do not fill** (they fill after completion). The representative-only detail list has the same cause.
- Decision: **DEFERRED** (functional builds first). Registered in the development-progress deferred backlog as "thumbnail priority/prefetch for pages first seen during a scan".
## 0.9.4.143 — Drop stale pairs of changed files + auto re-apply after a changed scan + recent-folder count

Field S-4: replacing a group member with a different image of the same name/similar size kept the old group after a Fast search (Test Mode was correct).
### Cause
- The worker saved quick-loaded stored pairs plus this scan''s emissions as one set, so stale pairs of re-analyzed files were never removed.
- The GUI union-find also kept the old edges.
### Changes
- Engine `ScanControl::onChangedFile`; worker `storedPairs_/storedCount_/changedFiles_`; persist drops stored pairs touching re-analyzed paths and keeps emitted pairs (checkpoints/final identical, telemetry uses the same set).
- GUI silently reloads the stored index after a scan that started with a result set and analyzed>0 (Test Mode excluded), preserving the summary/sort/selection.
- `ui/recentFolderLimit` (default 3, 1-20) with a Settings spin box; saving trims Favorites immediately.
### Verification
CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126. backend_e2e Test 1g (DB+GUI, checks=91), ui_settings keys.
### Impact
0.9.4.142 -> 0.9.4.143. Verdict-persistence correctness fix (schema/protocol/engine unchanged). Changed scans add one re-apply at completion.

## 0.9.4.151 — Audit finding fixes (adoption scope, cancel/fail consistency, save failure)

The 0.9.4.150 audit proved four confirmed defects.
### Changes
- A (partial-scope adoption deletion, P0): `AdoptScope` limits replacement to in-scope rows (upsert + scoped deletes, meta key upsert).
- B (cancel/fail/failure-only divergence, P1): changed-count propagation (CANCELLED 4th field, completion 7th, failure suffix) + re-apply on `analyzed>0 || changed>0`, failures too (error kept). Silent re-applies no longer clobber the status line.
- C1 (ignored save failure, P1): final failure emits `failed`, never success. C2 (checkpoint no-op, P2): `txActive_`+SAVEPOINT.
- Regression pins: e2e 1g2 (failure-only view consistency) / 1h (ignored+Yes preservation) / crash section 4 (injected failure yields failed, never finished) / new ui_date_sort CTest.
- One test-code defect fixed: building a `QSet` directly from temporary `QStringList` iterators SEGFAULTed; use a named local.
### Verification
CPU 126/126, GPU 127/127. 16 new checks pass verbose. `--version` 0.9.4.151 on all 4 binaries.
### Impact
0.9.4.150 -> 0.9.4.151. Judgement/schema/protocol unchanged. A final-save failure may leave committed file rows with the old match set — recoverable via Sequential/re-verify, and now visible.
## 0.9.4.152 — Directed re-review fixes (P0 content_hash key, P1 meta, save failure, checkpoints)

External re-review. P0 confirmed: adoption deleted from content_hash with a non-existent `path` column → any row to delete rolled back the whole adoption.
### Changes
- Explicit per-table key mapping: content_hash deletes use `rel` from the same `canonicalRelativePath` the writer uses. Unmappable rows are kept.
- Meta adopted on full scope only; partial keeps the main index's. The post-adopt production scan was observed running the full verification (`matchBaseline=forceFullPass` in the backend log).
- Save failure: `|msfChanged=N` + silent re-apply of the old set when N > 0 (view==DB) + baseline invalidation (next A/AB full re-verification) + retry.
- Checkpoint SAVEPOINT kept. Kill-durability claim withdrawn (unproven). File-row checkpoints stay valid.
- Regression pins: e2e 1h extended (deleted file rel removal + success, ignored preservation, baseline preservation, forceFullPass observed) / 1h2 new (locked adopt fails + full rollback verified + retry succeeds + full-scope baseline adopted) / ui_persist_fail new (reason delivered + view==DB + retry) / database savepoint.
- 1h2's g8 assertions use the g2 witness pair: g8 was modified in Test 1e, so the full re-verification legitimately unpairs it.
### Verification
CPU 127/127, GPU 128/128. New/extended checks pass verbose. `--version` 0.9.4.152 on all 4 binaries.
### Impact
0.9.4.151 -> 0.9.4.152. Judgement/schema/protocol unchanged. In-scan match kill durability unproven (separate design).
## 0.9.4.153 — Directed re-review P1-A/P1-B exit-path fixes

External re-review. P1-A: partial adoption on a valid baseline skipped the next full verification. P1-B: cancel/exception/engine-failure baseline lifecycle unsettled.
### Changes
- Delete `match_baseline` inside the partial-adopt transaction (full scope still upserts scratch meta). Rollback covers the delete.
- Invalidate the baseline on cancel / std::exception / non-std paths with applied changes (guarded try/catch). Engine-reported failure (`!r.completed`, not cancelled) emits `failed|msfChanged=N` with no results. Cancel branch first (a user cancel is never a failure).
- `MSF_TEST_ENGINE_FAIL` seam (deterministic engine-failure report), `testChangedCount` hook (deterministic cancel timing).
- Regression pins: new e2e 1h3 (valid baseline + partial adopt → invalidated → observed forceFullPass → restamped + pairs preserved/dropped) / crash §5 new (cancel after change approval → CANCELLED + invalidated + forced full pass + pair consistency) / §6 new (exception-path invalidation) / §4 extended (save-failure invalidation asserted) / database savepoint kept.
- One intermittent Test 1e (No-path) failure, then three consecutive full passes (identical binaries). The 1e path (test scan + No) never writes main and is unrelated to this change. Recorded as INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE with a failure-time row dump kept in the test. No speculative fix.
### Verification
CPU 127/127, GPU 128/128. New/extended checks pass verbose. `--version` 0.9.4.153 on all 4 binaries.
### Impact
0.9.4.152 -> 0.9.4.153. Judgement/schema/protocol unchanged. One full verification after a cancel/failure with changes. Kill durability still unproven.

## XMP full-corpus census + targeted production verification (post-0.9.4.153)

Close the I-XMP CONDITIONAL remainder (full-corpus coverage) with a read-only census plus isolated targeted production verification.
### Census (read-only; user index and dataset untouched)
- Scope: all of G:\Downloads\ss_twit — 174,012 JPEGs + 4,281 other rasters (png/webp/gif/avif/jpeg/jfif/jpe). Leading-64KB byte scan plus full-file phase 2 over every XMP carrier.
- Files carrying XMP packets: 1,189 (1,171 JPEG + 18 other).
- Files carrying `tiff:Orientation`: 106, all value 1 (identity). Zero non-identity values. Zero additional hits beyond 64KB in extended packets.
- EXIF coexistence (105 JPEGs): valid EXIF=1 in 101 (EXIF wins, XMP never consulted); invalid EXIF=0 in 3 (fall through to XMP=1 identity); no EXIF in 1 (XMP=1 identity). The PNG: no EXIF, XMP=1 identity.
### Targeted production verification (temp copy + build-tree index; user data untouched)
- Headless real-engine scan of the 105-JPEG copy: scanned=105 added=105 analyzed=105 failed=0 candidates=2 groups=1.
- After adding the PNG: scanned=106 added=1 analyzed=1 failed=0, existing pair kept.
- Conclusion: no file in the corpus can have its verdict altered by the XMP fallback (every value is identity and the EXIF-coexistence reading agrees). Together with fixture/18/79/134 real-file evidence plus test_mode_xmp_test, I-XMP real-world coverage is complete. CONDITIONAL close to be reflected in development-progress after user confirmation.

## 0.9.4.154 — Kill-durability D1 crash marker

Implementation of the D1 design (`docs/architecture/match-checkpoint-durability`). In-scan match checkpoints live in SAVEPOINTs inside the scan transaction, so a forced kill rolls back everything after the last engine commit; with a still-valid baseline the next A/AB skips full verification and the lost matches stay lost forever.
### Changes
- New `Database::scanDirty/setScanDirty` (`meta.scan_dirty` scalar upsert/delete, no schema change).
- `ScanWorker::run()` plants the marker in its own autocommit right after the index opens; a function-scope RAII guard (`SettledExit`, noexcept with internal try/catch) deletes it on every settled exit (complete/cancel/reported failure/exception unwind). Only a forced kill skips destructors, leaving the key set.
- The scan never reads the key itself. The first cut read it at scan start, saw the worker's own mark, and forced a full pass on every scan; walker_queue case H (`display-pending-full`) caught it. Fixed by having the worker read the pre-existing value and hand it over on `ScanControl::forceFullPass`, after which the full suites pass.
- `MediaSearchEngine::scan()` runs one forced full verification when `forceFullPass` is set, regardless of the baseline (`dirty=1` in the log), then restamps. A clean exit clears the key, so one crash costs exactly one full pass.
- Pins: new crash §7 (15 checks, no marker after clean scan → manual plant → `forceFullPass dirty=1` → restamp + marker gone + changed pair dropped + untouched pair kept). `ui_cancel_consistency_test` finalized (progress-signal gating instead of the fixed-sleep tail race). The e2e sqlite busy_timeout(10s) hardening rode in the earlier commit (778bcda).
### Verification
CPU 128/128, GPU 129/129. New and extended sections pass verbose. `--version` 0.9.4.154 on all 4 binaries.
### Impact
0.9.4.153 → 0.9.4.154. Judgement/schema/protocol unchanged. Forced-kill mid-write durability itself remains best-effort (WAL + single-transaction semantics).

Five consecutive post-release `msf_backend_e2e_test` runs failed 3 times: 1e twice with the known `rowBefore=""` signature, 1d once ("adopted" pump passed, then the equality check failed while "row actually changed" passed). - All three readers now print `sqlite3_errcode` as `[DBG] row read empty suffix=... err=...` on empty results, so any recurrence is classified by code (existing rowBefore/rowAfter dumps kept).

## External research: NVIDIA-GPU video decode projects (post-0.9.4.154, research only)

Survey of external projects using NVIDIA GPUs for video decode, harvested for patterns usable in continuous fingerprinting and search comparison. No adoption decision (order stays: HW phase after 1.0 Vulkan).
### Projects surveyed
- NVIDIA/video-sdk-samples (NvDecoder): zero-copy decode→CUDA interop as the canonical pattern.
- VPF → PyNvVideoCodec (successor, pip-installable, MIT, officially supported): HW decode + on-device Surface resize/convert kernels + zero-copy DLPack export. Windows supported. Pattern reuse only (Python-centric, unsuitable as a dependency; VPF archived 2024).
- nvvl → DALI (successor, open source): FFmpeg parsing + NVDEC decode + texture-unit scale/crop/flip straight into device-memory tensors. Sequence/keyframe-interval guidance reusable.
- akamhy/videohash: pure CPU/FFmpeg perceptual hash (1fps → 144px collage → wavelet XOR dominant-color). No GPU. Confirms the standard pipeline shape (frames → small thumbs → hash → Hamming); not a technical borrow target.
- FAISS: binary indexes (IndexBinaryFlat/IVF/HNSW, Hamming) + CUDA support. Future path for large-scale candidate KNN in search comparison; unnecessary at current scale (thousands) where the candidate index suffices.
### Applicable to our design
- Device-resident decode→preprocess: NVDEC → on-device NV12 → on-device convert/resize (96px gray + 32px + thumb48), removing swscale + CPU box-mean + H2D. All three projects converge on this pattern.
- Fingerprint kernels stay as-is (they already consume device buffers; zero-copy connects naturally). NVDEC output may differ byte-wise from FFmpeg SW, so F-1 exactness re-proof is a precondition.
- Search comparison stays as-is until the corpus grows 2–3 orders of magnitude; then revisit FAISS GPU binary Hamming.
### Constraints (unchanged)
- No build SDK, F-1 FAIL (1360x808 20/20) + F-2 prohibition, order after Vulkan. This entry is a harvest record, not an execution plan.
### Deep dive (follow-up)
- vcpkg FFmpeg already carries an `nvcodec` feature (`ports/ffmpeg/portfile.cmake:411`: `--enable-cuda --enable-nvdec --enable-cuvid --enable-ffnvcodec`). Its comment states `--enable-cuda` needs no CUDA SDK (runtime detection + dynamic loading). So the FFmpeg path (`-hwaccel cuda` + `scale_cuda` filter) opens with a vcpkg feature addition and no NVIDIA SDK on our machine. The "no build SDK" blocker applies to the native NvDecoder path only.
- NPP ships complete in the toolkit (headers + `nppi*.lib` verified): `nppiResizeSqrPixel_8u_C1R` (gray resize), `nppiNV12ToRGB_*` (NV12 conversion), `nppiFilterBoxBorder_8u_C1R` (box). Callable from our C++ with zero new dependencies — a better vehicle than CV-CUDA for on-device preprocessing.
- CV-CUDA excluded: active project (2.7k stars, cu13 wheels) but **no native Windows support (WSL2 only)**. Incompatible with our native VS18 build.
- NV12's Y plane is itself the full-res gray image. A device pipeline can go Y plane → NPP resize (96px → 32px) → existing pHash/SSIM kernels with no color conversion at all.
- `scale_cuda` converts format and scales while frames stay in device memory (needs hw device init + filter graph). Combined with an `nvcodec` FFmpeg build, device frames are reachable with no SDK.
- nvImageCodec (GPU JPEG decode + DLPack) recorded only as a future image-side candidate (Windows/toolkit inclusion unverified).
- Preconditions hold: device-resize output needs a parity gate against the CPU swscale box-mean, and NVDEC-decoded pixels may differ from SW decode, so F-1 exactness re-proof is required.
### Deep dive 2 — GPU decode in players/browsers (with local proof)

As pointed out, players and browsers all decode on the GPU by default. Patterns directly reusable in our design, verified by measurement:
- **D3D11VA works right now (zero new dependencies).** Measured with our vcpkg FFmpeg: `-hwaccel d3d11va` + H.264 → `Reinit context ... pix_fmt: d3d11`, 90 frames, 0 errors, 26.3x, frames kept in device memory. No h264_d3d11va wrapper exists, but the fixed-function decoder engages through the SW decoder's get_format hwaccel path. Unlike NVDEC it is **vendor-neutral** (Intel/AMD/NVIDIA), matching our vendor-neutral direction.
- **The D3D11 → CUDA zero-copy path is open.** `cuGraphicsD3D11RegisterResource` is present in the installed toolkit's `cuda.h`. D3D11VA decode → D3D11 texture → CUDA registration → straight into the existing pHash/SSIM kernels needs no new SDK (code only, ordered after Vulkan).
- **mpv pattern**: `--hwdec=auto` negotiation ladder (native → copy-back → SW fallback) + frames kept on-GPU into the libplacebo renderer. Isomorphic to our scheduler+fallback contract.
- **Chromium pattern**: per-driver blocklists disabling video_decode with SW fallback + `chrome://gpu` diagnostics. Same philosophy as our capability+calibration gating and "no support claim without validation".
- **Caveat**: HW-decoded pixels may differ byte-wise from SW (players assume GPU copies/fallbacks too), so adoption requires re-running the fingerprint parity gate (video_decode_parity_test pattern).

## 2026-10-31 — V: Video Content Matching Design Refinement and Pre-registration

The video duplicate-search discussion was reconciled with the current source and the closed Node E decision, then recorded as a separate V product-feature workstream. **This is a proposal/pre-registration, not an implementation or measurement result, and it is not in the Active Build Queue.**

### Main design refinements

- Separate whole-video duplicate search from partial-clip search. A 10-second short and a 2-hour film are not default whole-video candidates.
- The current 32-second plan requests about 245 positions for a 130-minute example, but the decoder seeks once and then sweeps sequentially to the final target. At 25 fps, output could be on the order of 195,000 frames by arithmetic. **This is not a measurement.** Measure actual cost through the 0.9.4.155 decodedFrames telemetry.
- 10–14 frames / center target 12 means retained representative images. Keep Probe/Kept/Decoded counts separate.
- For films, use opening probes over 0–30 seconds, main-content boundary search around 30 seconds–3 minutes, a few middle-core anchors, and reverse-time credit-boundary probes from T-15 seconds to T-20 minutes. Represent black/credit intervals as metadata.
- Down-weight common intros/logos/recaps/credits by library frequency. Never accept a long-form candidate from opening+ending matches alone.
- Use adaptive refinement of 1–2 frames only in distinctive core regions when candidates are ambiguous.
- Use horizontal mirroring only; vertical flip is excluded.

### Node / decoder boundary

Keep Node E's ExactnessPolicy::RefuseAll and production sparse-seek rejection. The first content-algorithm prototype validates kept-frame reduction and accuracy against the current sequential decoder. Do not claim an actual decodedFrames reduction until a separate random-access prototype passes decoder exactness and cost gates. Do not reopen Node E or bypass its production prohibition.

### Plan / Gates

- New implementation-briefs/V-video-content-matching.{ko,en}.md pre-registers V0 dataset/ground truth → V1 candidate-population separation → V2 structural probes → V3 representative frames → V4 temporal alignment → V5 separate partial-clip search → V6 production adoption.
- V is a separate proposed product-feature workstream outside the A-H mainline and remains DEFERRED. It does not replace XMP acceptance/S5 real-dataset benchmark priorities.
- No build version assigned. No implementation/test/engine/DB/cache change. No Build History entry is created because there is no product change or measurement.

## 2026-10-31 — V: GUI Video Settings Tab and User-Configurable Profiles

At the user's request, the video-content comparison design now includes a **Video tab** in Settings. This is a design update to the architecture and implementation plan, not a GUI or algorithm implementation.

### Settings UX and recommended defaults

- First-run default is **Automatic (recommended)** and preserves the internal G1–G8 duration cohorts and structure classification. The UI groups controls as Short-form / Mid-length / Long-form without force-classifying the 60s–25m range as either short or long.
- Short-form (up to 60s) recommends a **5-second full-timeline Probe interval**. A one-minute clip therefore has about 12 baseline observation positions; representative-frame centers are G1 (up to 15s) 5 (range 4–6) and G2 (15–60s) 8 (range 6–10).
- Long-form (over 25m) recommends **5-second structural-boundary detail** and **5-second main-content refinement** intervals. They apply only inside automatically selected opening/main-content-start/ending boundary windows or uncertain local core windows. Users can tighten the interval from 5s to 3s inside those windows. Uniform 3s/5s scanning of the entire film is not the recommended mode.
- Mid-length content keeps the existing structure-aware automatic cohort policy. Long-form retains 1–3 initial core anchors, cohort-specific representative-frame targets (9–12 for 25–60m, 10–14 for 60–150m, 12–16 over 150m), and 1–2 added frames per uncertain region.
- The initial proposed input range for Custom intervals is 1–60s; the final ceiling and per-file Probe/Kept budgets must be set by real-data cost/accuracy gates.

### Setting semantics and safety boundaries

- The UI label “Frame-check interval” means Probe timestamp spacing, not retained-frame count or actual decodedFrames. The 0.9.4.155 sequential decoder may output intermediate frames between targets, so a 5s-to-3s change must not be reported as decoder savings.
- Freeze effective settings in a run snapshot at search start; edits during a run apply only to the next search.
- Reflect fingerprint-affecting policy changes in cache freshness. Never silently mix fingerprints produced under different policies; do not assume a DB/schema/cache migration before reviewing the current cache contract.
- V stage sequence is now V0 dataset/ground truth → V1 candidate separation → V2 structural probes → V3 representative frames → V4 temporal verification → **V5 GUI Video Settings tab** → V6 separate Partial-clip → V7 Production adoption.
- Expose the GUI only after V0–V4 accuracy/cost gates pass. V remains DEFERRED and outside the Active Build Queue. No code/tests/version/DB/engine/cache change; no Build History entry is warranted.

## Record correction — RTX 3080 Ti AV1 hardware decode available (2026-11-02)

The earlier statement ("Ampere has no AV1 decoder, so dav1d is the only option") was wrong. Per NVIDIA's official article (RTX 30 series AV1 decoding), RTX 30 series GPUs carry dedicated AV1 hardware decoders up to 8K HDR. The RTX 3080 Ti (GA102, 5th-gen NVDEC) hardware-decodes H.264/H.265/VP9/AV1. Ada added AV1 *encode*.
- The dav1d choice stands (a software fallback is needed regardless), but the rationale is corrected: AV1 software decoding is due to (a) the F-1/F-2 policy block on hardware paths + (b) no cuvid/nvdec in the vcpkg FFmpeg (verified locally) — not a silicon limit.
- Enabling NVDEC needs F-1/F-2 revisit + an nvdec-capable FFmpeg build + fingerprint-equivalence validation against the software path first.

## f07 HW/SW mismatch detail (2-bit drift confirmed, accepted) — post-0.9.4.170 investigation

### Target file
- `D:/Temp/OpenCodeWork/msf_video_field/orig/f07.mp4` ← `G:\Downloads\ss_twit/cooc_h_-1429503298122099200-20210823_025839-vid1.mp4`
- 720x1232 H.264, yuvj420p full-range BT.709, 3.98 s.

### Comparison method
- Same-file SW (`MSF_VIDEO_HW=off`) vs HW (auto) full builds → kept hash/timestamp comparison.
- Scope: all 50 orig files + 1225 cross pairs + mixed-path duplicate pairs (f07 orig/reenc, orig/flip).
- Pixel level: direct 96x96 gray comparison at t=0/1/2/3/3.5/3.93 + Y-plane means + ham/ssim/final matrix dumps (`MSF_VIDEO_DUMP_MATRIX`).

### Problem manifestation
- Same kept count/timestamps (2 frames: 0, 3.93). Frame idx1 (t=3.93) differs by 2 hash bits (xor popcount=2).
- Y plane means bit-identical (79.2388 vs 79.2388). After gray conversion HW is +8.66 mean / max 21, 9065/9216 pixels differ.
- Sign flips by segment: HW -4.7 darker at t=0–2, +8 brighter after t=3.

### Cause tracing (per-hypothesis verdicts)
1. Time-penalty hypothesis → rejected. Dump shows zero passing final cells, SSIM max 8–30. No cells, not penalties.
2. Range-flag hypothesis → rejected. Post-transfer unspec confirmed; flag fixup leaves output unchanged.
3. Transfer-format hypothesis → rejected. Transfer output is NV12 (value 23). Direct YUVJ420P requests are refused by the driver and fall back to NV12.
4. Confirmed: sws NV12-vs-YUVJ420P chroma path difference. Identical Y + differing gray + sign flip is the signature of chroma resampling/coefficient difference. The format path, not the range flag, decides the conversion.

### Verdict
- 1225 cross pairs: bit-identical scores, 0 flips (at both 50 and 87.5). Mixed-path duplicates: delta ≤0.47, far from any verdict boundary.
- HW output deterministic (hwHwDiff=0). Not random jitter.
- Disposition: accept + monitor via telemetry. sws surgery rejected — regression risk to the 49 good files.
- Forced-conversion attempts and outcomes (all ineffective, reverted without shipping):
  1. Copying the range flag → no output change (sws ignores the NV12 input range flag).
  2. Direct YUVJ420P transfer request → refused by the driver, falls back to NV12 (identical output).
  3. sws_setColorspaceDetails(srcRange=full) forcing → output changes but flips sign (unconditional forcing looked like 0 diff on f07 but broke limited-range files; conditional forcing inverts the error). No runtime flag aligns the sws NV12 path with the SW yuvj420p path.
  4. CLI cross-check: same yuvj420p → NV12→gray (scale filter, no range flags) is bit-identical to SW; NV12+in_range=mpeg reproduces the +8.67 f07 pattern. So sws fixes NV12 input to the limited-range interpretation.
  Conclusion: decoded YUV values are identical (CLI Y/U/V ndiff=0); the difference lives entirely in the sws conversion stage. All safe levers tried and ineffective, so the validated 0.9.4.170 code stands. Revisit lead: the scale-filter path (explicit in_range) is exact, so routing HW frames through the same filter graph as SW is the way to retry.
- Forced-conversion attempts and outcomes (all ineffective, reverted without shipping):
  1. Copying the range flag onto transferred frames → no output change (sws ignores the NV12 range flag).
  2. Direct YUVJ420P transfer request → refused by the driver, falls back to NV12 (identical output).
  3. sws_setColorspaceDetails(srcRange=full) forcing → no change. With identical Y and sign-flipping deltas, the cause lies in the converter's NV12-vs-YUVJ420P chroma path, unreachable from runtime switches.
- The range/fixup and direct-YUVJ420P transfer requests all proved ineffective (output unchanged) and were reverted, not shipped. Recorded as a negative result.

## SW vs HW (D3D11VA) head-to-head — same 150-file dataset (2026-11-03)

Follow-up question (post-0.9.4.170): does DX schedule/distribute between CPU and GPU itself, and which of SW/NVDEC/HW is error-free and fastest.
### Code audit result
- DX (D3D11VA) is used ONLY for the decode stage in `VideoDecoder` (`av_hwdevice_ctx_create` once + `get_format` + `av_hwframe_transfer_data`). No VideoProcessor, no compute shaders, no DX-side scheduling.
- Scheduling/distribution is entirely ours (Adaptive Scheduler, worker threads, CUDA backend). DX only decodes and hands frames back to the CPU immediately.
- No native NVDEC API (cuvid) in the build (absent from vcpkg FFmpeg). On this PC the HW path == D3D11VA == NVDEC silicon (same path).
### Measurement (150 msf_video_field files, fresh full builds on both paths)
- Time: SW 1078.1 s vs HW 812.7 s = **1.33x**. hwUsed on 50/50 files.
- Fingerprints: 1/150 differs (f07, 2 bits, same file). Other 149 identical.
- Duplicate pairs (100): pass50=100/100, pass87=94/94 (identical SW/HW). maxDelta=1.40, flips=0.
- Cross pairs (1225): maxDelta=0, flips=0 (at both 50 and 87.5).
### Verdict
- **No errors**: SW/HW verdicts fully identical (duplicates and cross pairs, 0 flips).
- **Speed**: HW is 1.33x faster (only decode is HW; the rest is the same CPU path, so overall speedup is bounded).
- **Method choice**: keep HW default (with SW fallback). No DX-side scheduling exists, nor is it needed — the existing Adaptive Scheduler owns scheduling.

## Leading-blank (black leader) discrimination — L01-L05 (0.9.4.171 default/structured)

Ad/pre-roll scenario: does content with 30-60 s of black prepended still match, and does different content stay separated. Leaders: L01 45 s, L02 30 s, L03 60 s, L04 30 s, L05 45 s. Recipe: 720p mpeg4 (`scale=1280:-2,pad=1280:720` distortion-free, HDR `tonemap=hable` first) + AAC. `msf_video_field/lead/` + `lead_manifest.csv`. 20 files x default/structured runs (temporary harness, registration reverted).

### Results (50 / 87.5)

| Pair | Default | Structured | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| L01-lead x orig/reenc/flip | 7.7 | 7.7 | miss |
| L02-lead x reenc/flip (same 720p SDR pipeline) | 52.8/52.5 | 51.3/51.4 | DUP at 50, miss at 87.5 |
| L02-lead x orig (HDR) | 13.5 | 14.3 | miss |
| L03-lead x orig/reenc/flip | 6.1 | 8.3-8.4 | miss |
| L04-lead x orig/reenc/flip | 12.8 | 10.8 | miss |
| L05-lead x orig/reenc/flip (same geometry) | 48.8 | 48.8 | miss (borderline) |
| 10 lead cross pairs | all 0.00 | all 0.00 | separated (0 false positives) |

### Interpretation

- Even with identical pipeline and geometry, the leader alone collapses 99.9 to 6-53 (L05 45 s leader: 48.8 borderline; L03 60 s leader: 6.1). The current matcher does **not absorb a leading insertion** — under first-kept anchoring plus monotonic enforcement, a 30-60 s start offset breaks the whole alignment. Consistent with V-brief V4's unimplemented "piecewise alignment under insertions/deletions".
- Different content with leaders stays fully separated at 0.00 — leaders cause no false positives.
- Structured is neutral here (within +-2; confidence < 0.30 everywhere, fallback). Leaders further dilute V2 confidence (black prefix washes out scene statistics).
- Verdict: leading-ad robustness recorded as a **recall gap (miss)**. Belongs to V4 insertion alignment / V6 partial-clip scope; no default-path change, kept as follow-up.

| lead cross false positives@50 | 282 | 236 |
| lead cross false positives@87.5 | **16 (max 95.50, f02-f06)** | **0 (max 80.06)** |
| f02-lead vs f06-lead | 95.50 | 70.70 |

Interpretation: (1) same content + leader is a recall gap — 1-13 s of content behind 30-60 s of blank mostly misses (consistent with long-form L05's borderline 48.8). (2) different content + same leader is a precision gap — the shared black prefix produces identical flat-frame fingerprints, 16 false positives even at the production threshold. Structured removes FP@87.5 16->0 (variance floor + denser plan shave the shared flat part; f02-f06 95.5->70.7) at a small recall cost (20->18) — a measured precision/recall trade-off. No default-path change.

Recipe exceptions (f01 30/1, f02 exotic timebase unified to 30 fps) recorded in `lead_manifest.csv` and here.

### Leader vs original/flip false-alarm check (f01-f50 150 files, L01-L05 20 files)

Delayed (leader) duplicates compared against originals and horizontal flips for false detections. 150 files (50 orig + 50 lead + 50 flip) x default/structured + 60 L-set cross pairs.

| Pairs (default / structured) | DUP@50 | DUP@87.5 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| f orig-flip same | 50/50, 50/50 | 48/50, 47/50 | comparison itself valid |
| f lead-flip same | 20/50 | — | mostly miss |
| f lead cross (2450 ordered) | FP 52 -> 15 | FP **0 -> 0** | max 58.6 -> 70.4 |
| f flip cross | FP 0 -> 0 | FP 0 -> 0 | max 25.8 -> 13.0 |
| L lead vs other-content flip/reenc/orig, 60 pairs | FP 0 -> 0 | FP 0 -> 0 | max 3.19 |
| L flip cross | 0 | 0 | max 5.04 |

Verdict: (1) same-content leader-vs-flip 20/50 miss (recall gap; short content dwarfed by leader). (2) cross-content false alarms at the production threshold (87.5) are **all zero** — leaders/flips never merge different content. (3) at threshold 50, shared-leader FPs drop def 52 -> full 15 (structured precision gain). (4) orig-flip itself 50/50 DUP, comparison valid. No default-path change.

L 15 pairs: verdict DUP V1 12 = V2 12, scores 85/95→90/100, L02-lead V1 DIFF→V2 UNCERTAIN. f 50 pairs: verdict DUP 1→5 (U44→35, D5→10), score≥50 11→13, ≥87.5 0→10, cross 4900 pairs FP 0 both. Engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

### Long-form ad-insertion reading experiment (2026-11-06, measurement only)

New report `docs/field-reports/longform-ad-capture-efficiency.ko.md`. 5 works (30+ min), 20 pairs (5 black + 15 controlled-synthetic moving, 30/60/180 s), full 3 s capture + dense 1 s zones. Key measurements: full correspondence offsets exact 20/20; start search saturates at 300 s, N=2/3 tied, N>=4 collapses, tolerant 3-of-4 run 10->15/20; center rep3 56/60, ending rep3 57/60; interval sweep 1-2 s (start) to 3 s (center/ending, max 6 s); recommended extraction ~1000 frames/pair (~60-70% fewer). Strategy S3T+2of3: DUP 15 / UNCERTAIN 0 / miss 5, cross 240 pairs FP 0. Failure causes: L01 opening 81.2x4 (weak-evidence rule follow-up), L02 black HDR darkness, L03_ad30 boundary 81.2 (fixed by tolerance). Limits: real broadcast ads, 60-90 min / 120+ min bands, center-rep stride instability. No product-source changes, no commit.
